mainTopic: תשובה and כפרה: which sins need יום הכפורים, the ladder of atonement, חילול השם, and the greatness of תשובה
overview: The amud opens by asking whether תשובה alone atones for an ordinary לא תעשה, or whether it also needs יום הכפורים. Two sources seem to say that only לא תשא is severe, and the גמרא answers that this means 'לא תשא and everything like it.' A third source, from the verse at חורב, says outright that all other לאוין are cleared, so the גמרא concludes this is a dispute between תנאים. רבי אלעזר then shows from 'ונקה לא ינקה' that God clears those who do תשובה. Next comes רבי ישמעאל's ladder of כפרה. For an עשה, תשובה alone works. For a לאו, יום הכפורים is also needed. For כרת and מיתות בית דין, יסורין are also needed. For חילול השם, only death completes the כפרה. The גמרא then gives examples of חילול השם, such as a great person who delays paying or is seen without תורה and תפילין. It ends with אביי's ברייתא contrasting a learned person who makes ה׳'s name beloved with one whose dishonesty desecrates it. The amud closes with sayings on the greatness of תשובה, including the levels of תשובה out of love, out of fear, and through suffering.

steps.title: A source says only לא תשא is excluded from the light sins
steps.stepSummary: This is the end of a challenge. A source lists the light sins as עשה and לא תעשה, 'except for לא תשא.'
steps.simpleTranslation: ...except for 'You shall not take [God's name in vain]'!
steps.whatsHappening: This amud opens at the end of a challenge from the previous text. The source says every לא תעשה is a light sin, with only one exception: לא תשא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only לא תשא is left out, then every other ordinary לאו is a light sin that תשובה alone atones for. That goes against the view that a full לאו needs יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: the prohibition of taking God's name in vain
light sins, which תשובה alone atones for

phrases.english: except for 'You shall not take [the name of God in vain]'!
phrases.notes: The exclamation mark shows that this is the punch line of a challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a challenge that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a full לא תעשה is not atoned for by תשובה alone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leaving out only one לאו suggests that all other לאוין are light.

steps.title: 'לא תשא' means לא תשא and everything like it
steps.stepSummary: The answer reads the exception more broadly: לא תשא stands for its whole category of serious לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: [It means] 'You shall not take' and everything similar to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'לא תשא' in the source is an example of a category, not one single exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לא תשא is a full לאו that is punished by בית דין. So 'everything like it' includes all such full לאוין, and they are left out of the light sins too. With this reading, the source no longer contradicts the view.

phrases.english: 'You shall not take' and everything that is similar to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: an example stands for a whole category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only לא תשא is left out of the light sins.
steps.terutzMaskana: All full לאוין like לא תשא are left out of the light sins.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's ranking from לא תשא down and up
steps.stepSummary: A new source: according to רבי יהודה, anything 'from לא תשא and below' is atoned for by תשובה alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה says: For anything from 'You shall not take' and below, repentance atones. From 'You shall not take' and above, repentance holds off the punishment and יום הכפורים atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source to challenge the same view. רבי יהודה uses לא תשא as the dividing line between lighter and heavier sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumes that 'below לא תשא' includes all the other ordinary לאוין. If so, תשובה alone would atone for them, which goes against the view.

phrases.english: Come and hear: Rabbi Yehuda says:
anything that is from 'You shall not take' and below —
repentance atones;
from 'You shall not take' and above —
repentance holds off [punishment] and Yom Kippur atones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge on the same question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a full לאו needs יום הכפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Below לא תשא' seems to include every other לאו.

steps.title: The same answer: לא תשא and everything like it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away רבי יהודה's source with the same answer as before.
steps.simpleTranslation: [It means] 'You shall not take' and everything similar to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof using the same answer from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's dividing line is the whole group of full לאוין like לא תשא, not that one לאו alone. Only sins below that whole group are atoned for by תשובה alone.

phrases.english: 'You shall not take' and everything that is similar to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 the same way step 2 answered step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference drawn from רבי יהודה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge read 'לא תשא' as one single לאו instead of a category.

steps.title: The verse at חורב: God clears all other לאוין
steps.stepSummary: A third source learns from the verses that God does not clear the sin against His name, but He does clear all other חייבי לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Since it says at חורב about repentance 'and He clears,' you might think לא תשא is included with them. So the verse says 'He will not clear.' You might think the other לאוין are the same. So the verse says 'His name': it is His name that He does not clear, but He does clear the other חייבי לאוין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third source. This one directly names 'שאר חייבי לאוין' as cleared by תשובה, so the earlier answer cannot work here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'את שמו' limit the strict rule to לא תשא alone. The ברייתא then says outright that all other לאוין are cleared. Reading 'everything like it' is no longer possible, so this is a strong challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: סיני, where the תורה was given
people liable for all other prohibitions

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to use the 'וכל דדמי ליה' answer here. This ברייתא spells out 'שאר חייבי לאוין,' so that reading is ruled out. That is why the גמרא needs a new kind of answer.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
since it was said at Horeb regarding repentance 'and He clears,'
one might think that even 'You shall not take' is included with them —
the verse teaches: 'He will not clear.'

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף שְׁאָר חַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין כֵּן —
phrases.english: One might think that the other people liable for prohibitions are the same —
the verse teaches: 'His name':
it is [the sin against] His name that He does not clear,
but He does clear the other people liable for prohibitions.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, stronger challenge that the earlier answer cannot handle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a full לאו needs יום הכפורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא openly says that all other חייבי לאוין are cleared by תשובה.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits the ברייתא disagrees and shows another ברייתא that places a full לאו with the severe sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as it was taught: For what does repentance atone? For an עשה and for a לא תעשה that can be fixed by an עשה. For what does repentance hold off punishment and יום הכפורים atone? For כריתות, for death penalties of בית דין, and for a full לא תעשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חורב ברייתא is simply one side of a disagreement among תנאים. It then quotes a ברייתא from the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא lists 'לא תעשה גמור' among the sins that need יום הכפורים. So the view being challenged has its own תנא to lean on. The two ברייתות are not reconciled; they just disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: it is a dispute between תנאים
a prohibition that can be fixed by doing a positive מצוה
death penalties given by the court
a full prohibition (with no עשה to fix it)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels: (1) עשה and לאו הניתק לעשה: תשובה alone atones. (2) כריתות, מיתות בית דין, and, according to this ברייתא, a full לאו: תשובה holds off the punishment and יום הכפורים atones. (3) The חורב ברייתא disagrees and puts ordinary לאוין in level 1.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that whether an ordinary לאו needs יום הכפורים is a real dispute between תנאים, not something settled by one source.

phrases.english: It is [a dispute of] tannaim, as it was taught:
For what does repentance atone?

phrases.aramaic: עַל עֲשֵׂה וְעַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁנִּיתַּק לַעֲשֵׂה,
phrases.english: for a positive מצוה, and for a prohibition that can be fixed by a positive מצוה;

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל מָה תְּשׁוּבָה תּוֹלָה וְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים מְכַפֵּר —
phrases.english: and for what does repentance hold off [punishment] and Yom Kippur atone?

phrases.aramaic: עַל כָּרֵיתוֹת וְעַל מִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: for [sins punished by] karet and for court-imposed death penalties,
and for a full prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by admitting a dispute between תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חורב ברייתא proves that ordinary לאוין are light.
steps.terutzMaskana: Another תנא holds that a full לאו needs יום הכפורים, so the view stands with that תנא's support.

steps.title: Where do we see that 'ונקה' at חורב is about תשובה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the earlier ברייתא, that 'ונקה' was said at חורב, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: 'Since it was stated at חורב: ונקה.' How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the ברייתא it quoted earlier and asks how we know that 'ונקה' at חורב refers to תשובה. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumed that 'ונקה' is a promise to clear sinners who do תשובה. But the same verse also says 'לא ינקה', so it is not clear how 'ונקה' can be a promise of clearing. The גמרא wants the source for this reading.

keyTerms.meaning: חורב (סיני), where the י״ג מידות were said

phrases.english: The Master said:
Since it was stated at Horeb: "And absolve."
From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the back-and-forth about the ברייתא is settled, the גמרא returns to explain one of the ברייתא's own lines.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the source that 'ונקה' at חורב speaks about those who do תשובה?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: God clears those who repent
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר settles the clash between 'נקה' and 'לא ינקה': God clears those who repent and does not clear those who do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אלעזר says, you cannot read the verse as 'He clears', because it also says 'He will not clear'. And you cannot read it as 'He will not clear', because it also says 'He clears'. So how does this work? He clears those who repent, and He does not clear those who do not repent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. The two halves of the verse seem to contradict each other, so רבי אלעזר splits them between people who do תשובה and people who do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says 'ונקה לא ינקה', which seems to say both 'He clears' and 'He does not clear'. Neither half can cancel the other, so each half must apply to a different case. This proves that 'ונקה' is about תשובה, which is exactly what the earlier ברייתא needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How so?', the line that resolves the contradiction

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base source in the תורה that תשובה clears sin. It is the foundation for the whole discussion of כפרה that follows.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Elazar says:
It is impossible to say "absolve,"
since "will not absolve" is already stated,
and it is impossible to say "will not absolve,"
since "absolve" is already stated.
How so?
He absolves those who repent,
and does not absolve those who do not repent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse is split: 'נקה' is for those who do תשובה, and 'לא ינקה' is for those who do not.

steps.title: רבי מתיא בן חרש asks about four levels of atonement
steps.stepSummary: רבי מתיא בן חרש asks רבי אלעזר בן עזריה in Rome whether he heard רבי ישמעאל's four types of כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מתיא בן חרש asked רבי אלעזר בן עזריה in Rome: Did you hear the four kinds of atonement that רבי ישמעאל used to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא on the topic of תשובה. It opens with a question, which sets up the list of levels of כפרה that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new discussion: not just whether תשובה works, but how much it does for each type of sin. The question speaks of 'four' levels, and the answer will correct that number.

phrases.english: Rabbi Matya ben Ḥarash asked

phrases.aramaic: אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה בְּרוֹמִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya in Rome:
Have you heard the four distinctions of atonement
that Rabbi Yishmael used to expound?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַל רַבִּי מַתְיָא בֶּן חָרָשׁ אֶת רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה בְּרוֹמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the source that תשובה works to a ברייתא about how it works for different sins.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What are רבי ישמעאל's four levels of כפרה?

steps.title: Three levels, with repentance in each
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה answers that there are three levels, and תשובה is needed in every one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: They are three, and תשובה goes together with each one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה corrects the number of levels and sets one rule for all of them: תשובה is always needed. This introduces the detailed list in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other things that atone, such as יום הכפורים, יסורין, and death, never work without תשובה. Each level only adds something on top of תשובה. The 'fourth' level (חילול השם) is not counted as a separate level of its own here.

keyTerms.meaning: Repentance is needed together with each one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that יום הכפורים or יסורין atone by themselves here. In every level, תשובה must be there first.

phrases.english: He said: They are three,
and repentance is with each and every one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers and corrects רבי מתיא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: There are three levels, and every one of them needs תשובה.

steps.title: Level one: a positive commandment
steps.stepSummary: Someone who failed to keep a מצות עשה and does תשובה is forgiven right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone broke a positive commandment and repented, he does not move from there before he is forgiven, as it says: 'Return, you wayward children.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the first level: for an עשה, תשובה alone brings complete forgiveness, and it happens immediately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'he does not move from there' means the forgiveness is instant. The verse 'שובו בנים שובבים' continues 'I will heal your backsliding', which shows that healing comes right away when a person returns.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not move from there, meaning immediately

phrases.english: If one transgressed a positive commandment and repented —

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ זָז מִשָּׁם עַד שֶׁמּוֹחֲלִין לוֹ,
phrases.english: he does not move from there until he is forgiven,
as it is stated: "Return, you backsliding children."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the list of three levels promised in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an עשה, תשובה alone atones immediately.

steps.title: Level two: a negative prohibition
steps.stepSummary: For a לא תעשה, תשובה holds the punishment off and יום הכפורים completes the כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone broke a prohibition and repented, the repentance holds things off and יום הכפורים atones, as it says: 'For on this day He will atone for you, from all your sins.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second level: for a לאו, תשובה alone is not enough to finish the job. It holds the punishment back until יום הכפורים completes the כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תולה' means 'keeps on hold': the punishment is suspended but not yet erased. The verse about יום הכפורים shows that this day finishes the atonement for sins like these.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspends, holds the punishment on hold

phrases.aramaic: עָבַר עַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וְעָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה —
phrases.english: If one transgressed a prohibition and repented —
repentance suspends, and Yom Kippur atones.
As it is stated: "For on this day He will atone for you
from all your sins."

steps.triggerLanguage: עָבַר עַל לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וְעָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next, more serious level after the עשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a לאו, תשובה suspends the punishment and יום הכפורים atones.

steps.title: Level three: כרת and מיתות בית דין
steps.stepSummary: For sins of כרת or מיתת בית דין, תשובה and יום הכפורים only hold things off, and יסורין finish the cleansing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone did sins that carry כרת or death by בית דין and repented, תשובה and יום הכפורים hold things off, and suffering scrubs the sin clean, as it says: 'I will punish their sin with the rod, and their wrongdoing with plagues.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third level: for the most serious sins, even תשובה together with יום הכפורים only suspend the punishment. Suffering (יסורין) completes the כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each level up adds one more step before the כפרה is complete. Here יום הכפורים moves from 'atones' to only 'holds off', and יסורין become what finishes it. The verse about the 'rod' and 'plagues' is the source for this.

keyTerms.meaning: Sins punishable by כרת (being cut off)
Sins punishable by death from the court

phrases.aramaic: עָבַר עַל כָּרֵיתוֹת וּמִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין
phrases.english: If one transgressed sins of karet or court-imposed death
and repented —
repentance and Yom Kippur suspend,
and suffering scrubs clean.
As it is stated: "I will visit their transgression with the rod,
and their iniquity with strokes."

steps.triggerLanguage: עָבַר עַל כָּרֵיתוֹת וּמִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין וְעָשָׂה תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and most serious regular level.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For כריתות and מיתות בית דין, תשובה and יום הכפורים suspend, and יסורין complete the כפרה.

steps.title: The special case of desecrating God's name
steps.stepSummary: For חילול השם, תשובה, יום הכפורים, and יסורין all only hold things off. Only death completes the כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But someone who has חילול השם on his hands: his תשובה cannot hold things off, יום הכפורים cannot atone, and suffering cannot scrub him clean. Rather, all of them together only hold things off, and death scrubs him clean, as it says: 'And ה׳ of Hosts revealed Himself in my ears: This sin will not be atoned for you until you die.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with an exception above all three levels. For חילול השם, every means of atonement together only suspends the punishment, and only death finishes the כפרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the usual tools, alone, has no power here at all. Together they can only suspend the punishment. The verse in ישעיה says 'until you die', which shows that death is the final step.
steps.whatToRemember: Atonement goes up a ladder. For an עשה, תשובה alone works. For a לאו, תשובה and then יום הכפורים. For כרת or מיתת בית דין, תשובה and יום הכפורים, then יסורין. For חילול השם, everything only holds things off until death. תשובה is required at every level.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ladder is the classic source for the laws of כפרה, which are later brought by the רמב"ם in הלכות תשובה. It shows that חילול השם is treated as the most serious sin of all.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ חִילּוּל הַשֵּׁם בְּיָדוֹ —
phrases.english: But one who has desecration of the Name on his hands —
his repentance has no power to suspend,
nor does Yom Kippur have power to atone,
nor does suffering have power to scrub clean;
rather, all of them together suspend,
and death scrubs clean,
as it is stated: "And the Lord of Hosts revealed Himself in my ears:
This iniquity shall not be atoned for you
until you die."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ חִילּוּל הַשֵּׁם בְּיָדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the exception above the three regular levels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For חילול השם, all the means of atonement only suspend the punishment, and only death completes the כפרה.

steps.title: What does desecrating ה׳'s name look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a practical example of חילול השם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a case of desecrating ה׳'s name?
steps.whatsHappening: We just learned that חילול השם is so severe that only death completes its כפרה. Now the גמרא asks what this sin actually looks like, and it is setting up several answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The term חילול השם could sound like something huge and rare. The question pushes us to find concrete, everyday cases, which will turn out to be surprisingly small actions.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? / What does it look like?

phrases.english: What is the case of desecration of the Name?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the sin mentioned in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical definition or example of חילול השם.

steps.title: רב: taking meat without paying right away
steps.stepSummary: רב says that if someone like him took meat from a butcher and did not pay immediately, that would be חילול השם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: For example, someone like me, if I take meat from a butcher and do not give him the money right away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers with a personal example: if an important person like him buys meat and does not pay on the spot, that is חילול השם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The action is not actually stealing, since רב plans to pay. The problem is how it looks: people may think a great רב takes without paying, and learn that stealing is okay.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, someone like me (an important person)

steps.confusionAlert: רב is not saying that buying on credit is forbidden for everyone. The issue is a public figure whose behavior people will copy or misread.

phrases.english: Rav said: For example, someone like me,
if I take meat from a butcher
and do not give the money immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An important person who delays paying for purchased meat creates חילול השם.

steps.title: אביי limits רב's case to places where sellers don't come collect
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב's case is only a problem where the seller does not come later to collect payment.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They only taught this in a place where they do not come to ask for payment. But in a place where they do come to ask, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows רב's example. Delaying payment is only חילול השם where it is not normal for sellers to collect later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the local custom is for the butcher to come collect later, everyone understands the buyer is using credit, so nobody suspects theft. The problem depends completely on how the public sees the action.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of
They demand / come to collect payment
We have no problem with it

phrases.english: Abaye said: They taught this only
in a place where they do not come to collect,
but in a place where they do come to collect —
we have no problem with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies רב's example from Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Delayed payment is חילול השם only where sellers do not normally collect later.

steps.title: רבינא: מתא מחסיא is a place where sellers collect
steps.stepSummary: רבינא notes that his town, מתא מחסיא, is a place where sellers come collect, so delaying payment there is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: And the town of מתא מחסיא is a place where they come to collect.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא applies אביי's rule to his own town and says buying on credit there is not a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows אביי's rule in practice. Whether an action is חילול השם can change from town to town, based on local custom.

keyTerms.meaning: The town of מתא מחסיא (רבינא's hometown)

phrases.english: Ravina said: And the town of Mechasya
is a place where they come to collect.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: וּמָתָא מַחְסֵיָא אַתְרָא דְּתָבְעִי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies אביי's distinction from Step 17 to a real place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In מתא מחסיא, delayed payment is not חילול השם.

steps.title: אביי's careful way of paying two partners
steps.stepSummary: When אביי bought meat from two partners, he paid each one separately, then brought them together to settle the account.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אביי bought meat from two partners, he gave money to this one and money to this one, and then brought them together and did the calculation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how אביי himself acted carefully when paying. He made sure each partner saw that he paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אביי had paid only one partner, the other might think אביי took meat without paying. By paying both and then settling together, he avoided any suspicion, which is exactly the concern of חילול השם.

phrases.english: Abaye, when he bought meat from two partners,
would give money to this one and money to that one,
and afterward bring them together
and work out the calculation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how אביי avoided the kind of suspicion described in Steps 16-17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A public figure should pay in a way that leaves no room for suspicion.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: walking without תורה and תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that if someone like him walked four אמות without learning תורה and without wearing תפילין, it would be חילול השם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: For example, someone like me, if I walk four אמות without תורה and without תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second answer to what חילול השם is: a great sage walking even a short distance without תורה or תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a regular person this would not be a big deal. But people expect a leader like רבי יוחנן to always be connected to תורה and מצוות, so seeing him without them could lower respect for תורה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: For example, someone like me
who walks four cubits
without Torah and without tefillin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the question of Step 15, parallel to רב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A great sage walking four אמות without תורה and תפילין is חילול השם.

steps.title: יצחק דבי רבי ינאי: when friends are embarrassed by one's reputation
steps.stepSummary: יצחק דבי רבי ינאי says חילול השם is any case where a person's friends are embarrassed by what they hear about him.
steps.simpleTranslation: יצחק דבי רבי ינאי said: Anyone whose friends are embarrassed because of what is heard about him, that is חילול השם.
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives a broader, general definition: if your reputation embarrasses your friends, that is חילול השם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of one specific action, this gives a test anyone can use. If the people connected to you feel ashamed of how you are spoken about, you are bringing shame on ה׳'s name.

keyTerms.meaning: His reputation / what is heard about him

phrases.english: Yitzchak of the school of Rabbi Yannai said:
Anyone whose friends are embarrassed because of his reputation
(that is desecration of the Name).

steps.triggerLanguage: יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר: כׇּל שֶׁחֲבֵירָיו מִתְבַּיְּישִׁין מֵחֲמַת שְׁמוּעָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to Step 15, giving a general rule rather than a personal example.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A reputation that embarrasses one's friends is חילול השם.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: when people say 'May his Master forgive him'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says חילול השם is when people say about someone, 'May his Master forgive so-and-so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: For example, when people say, 'May his Master forgive so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth answer: חילול השם is when a person's behavior leads people to say he needs ה׳'s forgiveness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When people talk about a religious person as someone who needs forgiveness, they are saying his actions are wrong. His public image now reflects badly on תורה and on ה׳.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
For example, when people say:
May his Master forgive so-and-so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כְּגוֹן דְּקָא אָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer to Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When people speak of someone as needing ה׳'s forgiveness, that is חילול השם.

steps.title: אביי: the ברייתא on making ה׳'s name beloved
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא: 'You shall love ה׳' means making ה׳'s name beloved through learning, serving תלמידי חכמים, and dealing pleasantly with people.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said, as it was taught: 'And you shall love ה׳ your God,' meaning that שם שמים should become beloved through you. He should read תורה, learn משנה, serve תלמידי חכמים, and his business dealings with people should be pleasant.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by describing the opposite of חילול השם. He quotes a ברייתא that explains how a person makes ה׳'s name beloved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'love ה׳' as 'make ה׳ loved by others.' The recipe has two parts: being a real בן תורה, and being honest and pleasant in business. Understanding this positive picture helps us see what חילול השם is: the failure to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)

steps.confusionAlert: אביי's answer to 'what is חילול השם' is the whole ברייתא, not only this first half. The first half (Steps 23-25) describes the positive case of making ה׳'s name beloved. The second half (Steps 26-27) gives the actual case of חילול השם: a learned person who is dishonest in business and unpleasant with people.

phrases.english: Abaye said, as it was taught:
"And you shall love the Lord your God,"

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיְּהֵא שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם מִתְאַהֵב עַל יָדְךָ.
phrases.english: that the name of Heaven should become beloved through you.
That he should read Scripture and learn Mishnah
and serve Torah scholars,

phrases.aramaic: וִיהֵא מַשָּׂאוֹ וּמַתָּנוֹ בְּנַחַת עִם הַבְּרִיּוֹת,
phrases.english: and his business dealings with people should be pleasant,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fifth answer to Step 15, this time defining the sin through its positive opposite.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חילול השם is the reverse of making ה׳'s name beloved through תורה and honest, pleasant dealings.

steps.title: What people say about such a person
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא describes how people praise this person, his father, and his teacher, and say how fine his ways are because of תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do people say about him? Fortunate is his father who taught him תורה, fortunate is his teacher who taught him תורה. Woe to people who have not learned תורה. So-and-so, who learned תורה, see how pleasant his ways are and how proper his deeds are.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues, showing the public reaction to someone who learns תורה and acts kindly and honestly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People do not just praise the person; they credit תורה for his good character. This is the heart of קידוש השם: his behavior makes others wish they had learned תורה too.

phrases.english: What do people say about him?
Fortunate is his father who taught him Torah,
fortunate is his teacher who taught him Torah.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹי לָהֶם לַבְּרִיּוֹת שֶׁלֹּא לָמְדוּ תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Woe to the people who have not learned Torah,
so-and-so, whom Torah was taught —
see how pleasant are his ways,
how proper are his deeds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 23, showing the result of good conduct.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Good conduct by a בן תורה brings people to praise תורה itself.

steps.title: The verse: 'Israel, in whom I will be glorified'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a פסוק saying ה׳ is glorified through such a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: About him the verse says: 'And He said to me: You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes by quoting a פסוק from ישעיה that describes this person: ה׳ takes pride in him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the highest level, the exact opposite of חילול השם. A person who desecrates the Name brings shame on ה׳, while this person brings ה׳ glory.

keyTerms.meaning: I will be glorified / take pride

steps.whatToRemember: חילול השם is mainly about how a person's actions look to others, especially for a תלמיד חכם: not paying promptly, being seen without תורה and תפילין, or earning a bad reputation. Its opposite is a person whose learning and honest, pleasant dealings make people love תורה and ה׳.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sugya teaches that the more people look up to you, the higher your standard must be, because your behavior represents תורה to the world.

phrases.english: About him the verse says:
"And He said to me: You are My servant,
Israel, in whom I will be glorified."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Seals the ברייתא of Steps 23-24 with a פסוק.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A person who makes ה׳'s name beloved becomes one through whom ה׳ is glorified, the opposite of חילול השם.

steps.title: The learned person who behaves badly
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא now gives the opposite case. Someone learns תורה and serves תלמידי חכמים, but is dishonest in business and rude to people. People curse him, his father, and his teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: But someone who reads and learns and serves תלמידי חכמים, yet is not honest in business and does not speak pleasantly with people, what do people say about him? 'Woe to so-and-so who learned תורה, woe to his father who taught him תורה, woe to his teacher who taught him תורה. So-and-so who learned תורה, look how corrupt his actions are and how ugly his ways are.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא flips the earlier picture. It now describes a learned person whose bad behavior makes people speak badly of תורה. This half is אביי's actual answer to the question of Step 15, what חילול השם is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the exact mirror of Step 24. The תורה learning is the same, but the behavior is the opposite, so the praise turns into 'woe to him.' The point is that people judge the תורה itself by how its students act.

keyTerms.meaning: His business dealings (literally, his taking and giving)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not criticizing the learning itself. The learning is fine. The problem is that the learning is not matched by honest and pleasant behavior.

phrases.english: But one who reads Torah and learns משנה
and serves Torah scholars,
but his business dealings are not honest,
and his speech with people is not pleasant,
what do people say about him?
Woe to so-and-so who learned Torah.
Woe to his father who taught him Torah,
woe to his teacher who taught him Torah.
So-and-so who learned Torah:
see how corrupt his actions are
and how ugly his ways are,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מִי שֶׁקּוֹרֵא וְשׁוֹנֶה וּמְשַׁמֵּשׁ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with the positive case in Steps 24-25 and gives the opposite outcome.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תורה learner who is dishonest and rude causes people to curse him, his father, his teacher, and by implication the תורה itself.

steps.title: The פסוק about desecrating ה׳'s name
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends the negative case with a פסוק from יחזקאל: 'These are the people of ה׳, yet they left His land.'
steps.simpleTranslation: About him the פסוק says: 'When it was said of them: These are the people of ה׳, and they left His land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes the bad case with a פסוק, just as the good case closed with a פסוק in Step 25.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יחזקאל, the nations mock the Jews: 'These are ה׳'s people, yet they were exiled.' That kind of talk shames ה׳'s name. The learned person who behaves badly causes the same kind of shame, which is חילול השם.

keyTerms.meaning: And about him the פסוק says

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא gives two mirror cases. A learned person who is honest and pleasant brings קידוש השם, and people praise תורה. A learned person who is dishonest and rude brings חילול השם, and people curse תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the earlier definitions of חילול השם (Steps 21-22): the more a person is known as a תורה person, the more his behavior reflects on ה׳.

phrases.english: and about him the verse says:
"When it was said of them: These are the people of ה׳,
yet they left His land."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the negative case of Step 26 with a פסוק, parallel to Step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A תורה learner who behaves badly is an example of חילול השם, like the shame described in יחזקאל.

steps.title: תשובה brings healing to the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא says תשובה is great because it brings healing to the world, based on the פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא said: Great is repentance, because it brings healing to the world, as it says: 'I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main topic, תשובה, and starts a new series of 'great is תשובה' statements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the word 'ארפא' (I will heal) in the פסוק about returning. When people return to ה׳, the result is healing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said:
Great is repentance, for it brings healing to the world,
as it is said: "I will heal their backsliding,
I will love them freely."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of חילול השם and returns to praising תשובה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה is great because it brings healing to the world.

steps.title: Contradiction: are the sins wiped away or only healed?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר חנינא points out two פסוקים that seem to contradict. One calls the sinners 'שובבים' (wayward children), as if they were never real sinners. The other says 'I will heal your backsliding,' as if the sin is real and needs healing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר חנינא raised a contradiction. It is written: 'Return, wayward children,' meaning from the start you were only wayward. But it is also written: 'I will heal your backsliding'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חמא בר חנינא sets two פסוקים against each other. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling them 'children who wandered off' suggests their sins are treated like childish mistakes and erased completely. But 'I will heal' suggests the sin really happened and needs a cure. So which is it?

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction (literally, he threw one against the other)

steps.confusionAlert: Both quotes come from the same chapter in ירמיה (3:14 and 3:22), and they even share the words 'שובו בנים שובבים.' The contradiction is in the implication: wiped out completely versus healed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama bar Chanina raised a contradiction:
It is written: "Return, wayward children,"
meaning that from the start you were only wayward,
and it is written: "I will heal your backsliding"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the same speaker and the theme of healing through תשובה, now pointing out a tension between פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים in ירמיה about returning sinners.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק treats the sins as erased, like a child's mischief. The other treats them as real wounds that need healing.

steps.title: Answer: love versus fear
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק that erases sin completely is about תשובה out of love. The פסוק about healing is about תשובה out of fear.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is out of love; there it is out of fear.
steps.whatsHappening: The contradiction is solved by saying each פסוק describes a different kind of תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תשובה out of love is so powerful that the sins are treated as if they were only childish wandering, and they are wiped away. תשובה out of fear brings forgiveness, but the sin is still something that had to be 'healed.'

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there (each source speaks about a different case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the well-known idea, developed later on this דף, that תשובה out of love is on a higher level than תשובה out of fear.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: here it is out of love,
there it is out of fear.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן מֵאַהֲבָה כָּאן מִיִּרְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction of Step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: each פסוק refers to a different level of תשובה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that both פסוקים describe the same תשובה and disagree about its effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: תשובה out of love wipes away the sin completely (שובבים). תשובה out of fear brings healing of a sin that still counted (ארפא).

steps.title: Contradiction: can everyone return, or only a few?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה raises another contradiction. One פסוק says that whoever returns will be healed, which sounds open to all. Another says ה׳ will take 'one from a city and two from a family,' which sounds like only a few.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה raised a contradiction. It is written: 'Return, wayward children, I will heal your backsliding.' And it is written: 'I am a master over you, and I will take you, one from a city and two from a family'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה sets up a second contradiction between פסוקים about תשובה. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק suggests that healing depends only on returning, so it is open to everyone. The second פסוק suggests that only a small number of people will be brought back. These seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: I am a master over you

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda raised a contradiction:
It is written: "Return, wayward children,
I will heal your backsliding,"
and it is written: "I am a master over you,
and I will take you, one from a city
and two from a family"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel contradiction by a different אמורא, using the same 'רמי' pattern.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק makes healing available to anyone who returns. The other limits it to a few individuals.

steps.title: Answer: love or fear versus suffering
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the 'few' are those who return out of love or fear, which is rare. Returning through suffering is something everyone comes to.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here it is out of love or fear; there it is through suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה solves his contradiction by again pointing to different kinds of תשובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a few people return to ה׳ by choice, out of love or fear, so 'one from a city' fits them. But when suffering comes, everyone thinks about returning, so the open-to-all פסוק fits תשובה through suffering.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'love' and 'fear' are grouped together as the higher, rarer kind. In Step 30 they were split apart. Each step is comparing different levels.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels of תשובה: out of love (highest, sins wiped away), out of fear (sins healed), and through suffering (common, which everyone reaches).

phrases.aramaic: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן מֵאַהֲבָה אוֹ מִיִּרְאָה,
phrases.english: It is not difficult: here it is out of love or fear,
there it is through suffering.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא כָּאן מֵאַהֲבָה אוֹ מִיִּרְאָה כָּאן עַל יְדֵי יִסּוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction of Step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by the motivation for תשובה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed the פסוקים disagree about how many people can do תשובה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Few people return out of love or fear ('one from a city'). Everyone returns through suffering ('I will heal').

steps.title: תשובה reaches the כסא הכבוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי says תשובה is great because it reaches all the way up to the כסא הכבוד, learned from 'Return, Israel, until ה׳ your God.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: Great is repentance, for it reaches up to the כסא הכבוד, as it says: 'Return, Israel, until ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another 'great is תשובה' statement, this time from רבי לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is the word 'עד' (until). The פסוק does not just say 'return to ה׳.' It says 'return until ה׳,' which teaches that תשובה rises all the way to ה׳'s throne.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמַּגַּעַת עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד,
phrases.english: Great is repentance, for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory,
as it is said: "Return, Israel,
until ה׳ your God."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁמַּגַּעַת עַד כִּסֵּא הַכָּבוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the series of 'גדולה תשובה' statements that began in Step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשובה is great because it reaches the כסא הכבוד.
